concerns.concern: The temperature data are too sparse to show a step at T_N. No points lie between 150 and 200 K, and the 5.5% figure is just the difference between two single points. Dense sampling, cooling and warming runs, repeats and several flakes are needed.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b has seven points with no data between 150 and 200 K, i.e. across T_N ≈ 155 K.

concerns.concern: At nominally identical room-temperature conditions, the velocities in Fig. 3b and Fig. 4 differ by about 4%, which is as large as the claimed anomaly. This points to systematic run-to-run uncertainty (including angle uncertainty) that the error bars leave out.
concerns.quote: This ~4% discrepancy is the same order as the reported anomaly. It indicates systematic run-to-run uncertainty

concerns.concern: The velocity rises by an unusually large ~3.2% between 300 and 200 K, and points scatter noticeably in the AFM phase. The step should be quoted relative to a fitted anharmonic baseline, with an uncertainty, not relative to the single 200 K point.
concerns.quote: That is unusually large for anharmonic stiffening and is itself more than half the claimed anomaly.

concerns.concern: The mode partly samples the amorphous SiO2 layer, whose moduli decrease on cooling. This could lower the velocity without any magnetic involvement, and no temperature-dependent measurement on a bare SiO2/Si substrate is shown.
concerns.quote: Its elastic moduli decrease upon cooling below room temperature (anomalous dc/dT), which directly affects a mode partly carried by the 300 nm oxide.

concerns.concern: An adsorbate or condensate layer forming in the cryostat could mass-load the surface, lowering the frequency and the scattered intensity. Vacuum conditions and the warming/cooling protocol are not reported.
concerns.quote: A layer forming on the sample in the cryostat mass-loads the surface. This lowers the Rayleigh frequency and also reduces scattered intensity

concerns.concern: Thermal-mismatch strain, partial delamination or changes in van der Waals contact at the flake/SiO2 interface could change the boundary condition, while the FEM assumes perfect bonding.
concerns.quote: Thermal-mismatch strain, partial delamination, or changes in vdW contact at the flake/SiO2 interface would alter the effective boundary condition.

concerns.concern: Cold-finger contraction could move the laser spot to a region of different thickness or tilt the sample, causing shifts of tens of m/s. Spot position should be verified by imaging at each temperature.
concerns.quote: Cold-finger contraction can move the spot to a region of different thickness or tilt the sample.

concerns.concern: The BMS laser power and spot size are not reported. Local heating at typical mW-level power could shift the true sample temperature by tens of kelvin, so a power-dependence test is needed.
concerns.quote: BMS typically uses mW-level power, far above the 0.024 mW used for Raman, so local heating could shift the true temperature by tens of K.

concerns.concern: T_N is not independently confirmed on the measured flake, since the authors' own Raman data show no clear anomaly. A sharp magnetic marker (exciton photoluminescence or magnon Raman) under BMS-like illumination is needed.
concerns.quote: The authors' own Raman data show no clear anomaly, so they cannot pin T_N.

concerns.concern: The proposed mechanism does not match the authors' own DFT. The Rayleigh velocity is said to be controlled by c33 and c44, yet DFT gives c44 unchanged, while the observed drop would need about an 11% cut in an interlayer shear modulus despite weak interlayer exchange.
concerns.quote: Yet DFT gives c44 unchanged (9.7 GPa in both states) and c33 reduced by ~8%.

concerns.concern: There is no estimate of whether the known exchange constants, or Ehrenfest-type thermodynamic relations using the specific-heat anomaly and dT_N/dε, could produce the required ~1 GPa change in c44. If they fall far short, the magnetic interpretation is in doubt.
concerns.quote: If these estimates fall far below 11%, the magnetic interpretation is in doubt.

concerns.concern: The abstract claims DFT+FEM reproduce the dispersion and the magnetic shift. In fact the calculated shift is 0.54% versus 5.5%, the absolute frequency is about 10% too high, and the velocities are off by 150–250 m/s.
concerns.quote: The calculated shift is 0.54%, an order of magnitude below experiment.

concerns.concern: There is no comparison with non-magnetic isostructural flakes (ZnPS3/CdPS3) or other MPS3 compounds with different T_N. Such controls would show whether the anomaly tracks each material's own T_N.
concerns.quote: Ideally, the same measurement on a non-magnetic isostructural flake (ZnPS3 or CdPS3) of similar thickness.

concerns.concern: The q-dependence of the anomaly, the most discriminating test between a film origin and a substrate/interface origin, has not been measured. The full dispersion above and below T_N, along different directions and on different thicknesses, is requested.
concerns.quote: The q-dependence of the anomaly is the most discriminating test and is missing.

concerns.concern: The DFT uses plain PBE-D3 with no Hubbard U and no statement on spin–orbit coupling. This is known to misdescribe the gap, moments and exchange of Ni2+ in NiPS3.
concerns.quote: Methods list plain PBE-D3 with no +U and no statement on spin–orbit coupling.

concerns.concern: The non-magnetic DFT state removes local moments entirely, so it is not a valid stand-in for the paramagnet and conflates loss of moments with loss of order. A disordered-local-moment or SQS reference and other ordered configurations are needed.
concerns.quote: The NM–AFM comparison therefore conflates loss of local moments with loss of order.

concerns.concern: The mode assignment is uncertain. Sezawa guided modes expected in this frequency window are not seen, and no scattering cross-section or polarization is given. A crossing or hybridization with another branch could produce apparent shifts or the intensity loss.
concerns.quote: Sezawa guided modes with sizable u_z are expected in the 2–7 GHz window and are usually observed.

concerns.concern: The 80–120 K peaks are weak, broad and sit on a sloped background, but fits are not shown. Fit details, linewidth and intensity versus temperature, and a discussion of the intensity collapse are requested.
concerns.quote: In Fig. 4a, the 80–120 K peaks are weak and broad and sit on a strongly sloped background.

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic formula uses the uniform susceptibility, which is small and continuous at T_N in an antiferromagnet. Landau theory instead predicts a step tracking the staggered order parameter squared.
concerns.quote: It writes c_eff = c0 − λ²χ_m with the uniform susceptibility.

concerns.concern: The magnetoelastic discussion mixes an exchange-striction picture with a single-ion coupling form without reconciling them.
concerns.quote: The text combines an exchange-striction picture (strain coupled to S_i·S_j) with a single-ion form

concerns.concern: Inferring an ~11% modulus reduction from v ∝ √c ignores that the mode depends on several elastic constants and on the substrate, as the authors stress elsewhere.
concerns.quote: Using v_R ∝ √(c_eff/ρ) to infer "~11% modulus reduction" ignores the multi-constant, substrate-dependent nature of the mode

concerns.concern: The described nearly constant velocity below T_N conflicts with the expected continued softening scaling with M², and with the precursor softening above T_N expected in a quasi-2D magnet. The current sampling cannot test either.
concerns.quote: The Landau picture predicts continued softening below T_N, scaling with M², rather than the "nearly constant" behaviour described.

concerns.concern: The DFT supercell dimensions do not obviously match a 1×4×2 multiple of the conventional C2/m cell. k-mesh convergence and the effect of zigzag order on the symmetry used in the strain set are not shown.
concerns.quote: The quoted dimensions (11.50 × 19.91 × 12.31 Å) are not obviously a 1×4×2 multiple of the conventional C2/m cell

concerns.concern: It is unclear whether the monoclinic DFT tensor was rotated so that z is the layer normal in the FEM model.
concerns.quote: the monoclinic c axis is not normal to the layers, so the tensor must be rotated so that z is the layer normal

concerns.concern: Key FEM inputs are missing: NiPS3 density, SiO2/Si parameters and their temperature, Si orientation, convergence with Si thickness and boundary, flake thickness uniformity, and sensitivity to thickness.
concerns.quote: the NiPS3 density; SiO2 and Si parameters, and the temperature at which they are taken

concerns.concern: The ripple-scattering selection rule is misstated. Loudon's mechanism needs a displacement component normal to the surface, not perpendicular to the propagation direction.
concerns.quote: Loudon's surface-ripple mechanism requires a displacement component normal to the surface, not "perpendicular to the propagation direction" as stated.

concerns.concern: Prior reports of elastic or mechanical signatures of magnetic order in MPS3 are omitted, including nanomechanical resonators, thermal expansion and the authors' own earlier BMS work. The claim that the acoustic response is unknown should be qualified.
concerns.quote: These should be discussed, and the statement that the acoustic response "remains unknown" should be qualified.

concerns.concern: Calling the effect giant and rarely reported is not justified, since several-percent elastic anomalies at magnetic transitions are common in bulk antiferromagnets.
concerns.quote: "Giant" and "rarely reported" should be justified quantitatively against such cases.

concerns.concern: The spin–phonon coupling constant cited from Ref. 49 refers to optical phonons, so citing it as agreement with an acoustic elastic anomaly needs justification.
concerns.quote: Its spin–phonon coupling constant refers to optical phonons. Citing it as agreement with an acoustic elastic anomaly needs justification.

concerns.concern: The claim that optical phonons are insensitive partly conflicts with prior reports. The missing ~176 cm⁻¹ splitting should be discussed in terms of thickness, resolution and polarization.
concerns.quote: The claim that optical phonons are insensitive is partly at odds with prior reports (refs. 16, 25, 30).

concerns.concern: Fig. 2d shows a visible FWHM change near T_N for the 255 cm⁻¹ mode, which should be quantified rather than dismissed as within uncertainty.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2d shows a visible FWHM change near T_N for the 255 cm⁻¹ mode. This should be quantified

concerns.concern: The guide-to-eye curve in Fig. 4b implies a smooth maximum near 210 K that the data do not resolve. It should be removed or replaced with a fitted baseline.
concerns.quote: The guide-to-eye curve in Fig. 4b implies a smooth maximum near ~210 K that the data do not resolve.

concerns.concern: BMS acquisition details are missing: acquisition times, free spectral range, contrast, collection optics/NA (which broadens q) and cryostat window effects.
concerns.quote: Specify BMS acquisition times, free spectral range, contrast, collection optics/NA (finite NA broadens q), and cryostat window effects.

concerns.concern: The Raman spectral resolution is not given, although the claimed absence of splitting depends on it.
concerns.quote: Specify the Raman spectral resolution, since the claimed absence of splitting depends on it.

concerns.concern: The softening is quoted inconsistently as ~5.5% in some places and ~6% in others.
concerns.quote: The softening is quoted as "~5.5%" in the abstract and conclusions but "~6%" on pp. 15 and 17.

concerns.concern: The Raman temperature range is stated differently in the text (90–290 K) and in Methods (77–300 K).
concerns.quote: The Raman temperature range is 90–290 K in the text and 77–300 K in Methods.

concerns.concern: Fig. 2a axes are mislabeled, and Fig. 4b misspells 'Temperature'.
concerns.quote: Fig. 2a axes are mislabeled: the x-axis reads "Temperature (K)" and the y-axis "Raman Shift (cm⁻¹)". Fig. 4b reads "Temperaure".

concerns.concern: Methods says 'electrodynamic' equation where 'elastodynamic' is meant.
concerns.quote: Methods says "linear electrodynamic equation"; this should be elastodynamic.

concerns.concern: 'REFERENCES' is misspelled, and Ref. 19 has a garbled author list.
concerns.quote: "REFRENCES" is misspelled. Ref. 19 has a garbled author list.
